title: OpcOS component registry
description: Central catalog of EVERY component installed on a machine (plugins, skills, MCP servers, offline tools, pipelines, products). Unlike an upstream/provenance manifest (which only tracks external sources), the registry answers: what does this machine have, what is it for, when do I use it, how does a new machine install it, and how important is it. Human-readable views (REGISTRY.md, docs/registry.html) are GENERATED from this file — edit here, never edit the generated files.

updated.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the last registry edit.

layers.description: The platform layers, bottom to top, used to render the layer diagram.

id.description: Layer identifier. The conventional set is: tool, governance, plugin, mcp, offline, pipeline, product.

desc.description: One-line description of what lives in this layer.

components.description: One entry per installed (or deliberately tracked) component. A component with no entry here is drift — a bug.

category.description: Which layer the component belongs to.

priority.description: Install priority for a new machine: core = install immediately; recommended = install unless the machine doesn't have that role; optional = install only on real need; deprecated = do not install / awaiting cleanup.

storage.description: The 3-branch storage law. adopted-in-repo = cherry-picked AND modified, lives inside the OpcOS repo (an upstream pull would overwrite your edits, so you own the copy). vendored-outside = whole repo / path-bound / has a runtime, cloned outside the repo; your patches live in vendor-adapt/ inside the repo. store = installed from the tool's first-party marketplace; the registry only records it. homegrown-in-repo = self-written, small text, lives in the repo. homegrown-outside = self-written but heavy (venv / models / output), lives outside in a well-known folder family.

location.description: Where the component lives on disk (use ~ or $HOME, never absolute user paths) or which store hosts it.

upstream.description: Origin: owner/repo for external sources (with license note), or 'homegrown' for self-written components.

purpose.description: What the component does — one or two sentences.

when_to_use.description: The trigger: which situations call for this component (and any role-split notes versus similar components).

install.description: How a new machine installs it: exact command, script, or pointer.

update.description: How it is kept up to date (store / package manager / cherry-pick / in-place edit).

size.description: Optional approximate disk footprint (e.g. '250MB', '4.5GB') — record it for heavy components so cleanup decisions are informed.
